title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v96
author: Priya Shah
description: Add adaptive-batching reporting pipeline and representative workload runners to Benchmark Lab. Motivation: enable automated collection of adaptive-batching microbenchmarks and end-to-end reporting so we can make data-driven batching and routing decisions for Redwood inference runtime (related to ENG-7890, ENG-7901). This PR wires up workload runners for token-level mixed workloads, adds profiling baselines for adaptive batch sizes, and introduces a reporting pipeline that normalizes latency/p99/cost across runs and pushes results to the performance metrics store. Changes include new workload definitions, a lightweight runner harness, ETL jobs for aggregation, and Grafana dashboard provisioning. Checklist: 1) Add representative workload runners (text-gen/chat/short-context/multi-turn) - done; 2) Add profiling baselines for adaptive batching (single-GPU and multi-GPU) - done; 3) Implement reporting pipeline (Airflow DAG + BigQuery export + metrics normalization) - done; 4) CI smoke + perf regression gates - updated; 5) Docs and runbook - added draft. Notes: kept diffs small and modular to ease review; performance-critical code isolated under benchmark-lab/runners and benchmark-lab/profiling. Linear: ENG-7890, ENG-7901. Related PRs: pr-362456, pr-401234, pr-420999.

summary: This PR adds end-to-end support for collecting and reporting adaptive-batching benchmarks in the Benchmark Lab. It includes runners, baselines, reporting DAGs, and dashboards so infra and runtime teams can iterate on batching policies with reliable data.
